# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about the communication structure here.

- I (Mute) can read the manual but cannot speak, and cannot touch the bomb.
- Blind can reach the bomb but cannot see or hear (well, Blind can hear speech from others, per the "cannot see anything printed or gestures" restriction — let me recheck).

Actually checking the table: Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" — so Blind cannot receive gestures, but presumably can hear speech. Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" — so Deaf cannot hear speech, but can see gestures.

I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives gestures. I cannot speak, so Blind can never receive anything from me directly. Blind must get info from Deaf (who speaks) after Deaf receives my gestures.

Turn order: Blind, Mute, Deaf. So this round: Blind spoke (I haven't seen it yet, arrives next round), then me now, then Deaf.

My job: communicate the manual (light->wire color mapping) to Deaf via gestures, so Deaf can then combine with what they see (the light color) and speak the correct wire color to Blind next round.

I need a gesture encoding for the manual. Let me assign symbols to colors, using distinct gestures per color, sending pairs (light, wire).

Let me use:
- blue = 👍
- green = ✌
- red = 👌
- white = ✋
- yellow = 🖐

I'll gesture the full mapping to Deaf now, since nothing depends on Blind's message yet (I haven't received it).

Since I have no context yet from Blind, I'll just send the manual encoding to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✋","✌","✌","👌","👍","✋","🖐","🖐","👌"])
```

TURN 2

|---|---|

| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb shows: display 0, light yellow, five wires in order: green, white, red, yellow, blue. I did not hear anything from you since I cannot hear. Please gesture only. Suggest gesture code: count fingers raised 1 to 5 using symbols ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐 for numbers 1-5, and 👌 for 0, so you can signal which wire number or answer numeric questions to me, and I will relay to Blind by speech.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0, light yellow, wires in order 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Waiting for manual instructions before cutting anything.

Now I have the key info: light is yellow, and wires in order are 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

From the manual: yellow → cut wire color red. Looking at the wire order, red is wire #4... wait let me recheck: wires are 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Red is wire #3.

Deaf suggested a numeric gesture code: ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐 for 1-5, 👌 for 0. I'll use that since Deaf proposed it and can see it clearly. I need to tell Deaf which wire number to cut, so Deaf can speak it to Blind (since I can't speak to Blind directly, and Deaf can't hear anything I "say" anyway, but Deaf can hear Blind and speak to Blind).

Wait, actually Deaf cannot hear - Deaf can only receive gestures from me. Deaf can speak though (Deaf isn't mute). So Deaf can relay to Blind by speech, as Deaf said.

So I need to gesture to Deaf: "cut wire number 3". Using the proposed code: 🤟 = 3.

I'll confirm the mapping and send the number.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 👍]

Deaf gestured back to me: [🤟 👍]. Using the numeric code (☝✌🤟✋🖐 = 1-5, 👌=0), 🤟=3, and 👍 isn't part of that code — 👍 might be Deaf's way of confirming/acknowledging ("got it", thumbs up), or it could be Deaf echoing back my signal for confirmation and adding a "yes/confirm" gesture.

Given light=yellow → cut red, and red is wire #3, my gesture of 🤟 (=3) was correct. Deaf echoing 🤟 back with 👍 likely means "confirmed, wire 3, understood" - acknowledging receipt before relaying to Blind by speech.

I have nothing new to add. I'll wait, or send a confirming gesture back to close the loop.

```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 👍 👎]

Deaf now sent [🤟 👍 👎] - this could mean Blind reported a problem after being told to cut wire 3, or Deaf is asking me to reconfirm. The 👎 is concerning - it might mean Blind said something didn't match, or Deaf is unsure and wants me to re-verify.

Let me double check my mapping: light yellow → manual says cut wire color RED. Wires in order: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. So red = wire #3. This is correct.

The 👎 might mean Deaf hasn't yet gotten confirmation from Blind, or something else went wrong (maybe Blind already cut a wrong wire, or display changed). Since I don't have speech access to know what's happening with Blind, I should just reaffirm my answer clearly to remove ambiguity - gesture the number 3 again plus a clear "confirm/yes" signal, avoiding any negative gesture that could be misread.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","👍"])
